# A link between two apps

<!-- generated by `python -m quality.sdk --reference`; edit the source, never this -->

One app's row names another app's row. Which form the link takes, the three lines a foreign key needs, and where the decision is written.

## Which form

- **A foreign key** — your row names the other app's row for as long as it exists, in the one tenant, and the database must refuse a delete that would orphan it — `ForeignKey("<app>.<Noun>", on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="+")`; across two apps it is `PROTECT`, because `CASCADE` is for a child of its own aggregate in its own app and a cascade across apps deletes rows the other app never sees (`django-architect` D2; `on_delete` is explicit, house rule 15) (`quality/rules.yaml:1774`)
- **An id, read through a selector** — your row mentions the other row but must not hold it in place — a `uuid` field (`scaffold field <app> <Noun> <name>:uuid?` writes one through every door) and the other app's `get_<noun>` at read time, whose `NotFound` you answer; it is still an import, so it still takes `depends_on` (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:130`)
- **An event** — the other app must learn that something happened, not name your row — `emit()` inside your service and no import either way; today an event reaches webhook endpoints and the socket bridge ([Events out](events-out.md)) and nothing subscribes in code, so an app that must ACT on another app's write has no in-process road on this tree: that is a lead's question, never an import (`apps/events/services.py:13`)

## A foreign key in three lines

- **1. The field** — on your model, the string form `"<app>.<Noun>"` so `models.py` imports nothing sideways, `related_name="+"` so the other model grows no reverse accessor and the arrow stays one-way (`apps/example_portal/models.py:55`)
- **2. `depends_on`** — on the IMPORTING app only — `depends_on += ("<app>",)` in your `apps.py`; the other app's declaration does not move, and the arrows stay a DAG (`apps/core/management/app_template/apps.py-tpl:13`)
- **3. The migration, inside the rung** — `uv run python manage.py makemigrations <your app>` — it depends on the other app's latest migration; never `makemigrations --merge`, which means two rungs touched one app (`quality/rules.yaml:13634`)

## Reading and writing across it

- **Read the other row through its selector** — `apps.<app>.selectors.get_<noun>(...)`, never your relation or its manager — your app learns nothing of the other noun's shape (`apps/example_portal/selectors.py:17`)
- **A row handed to your service was reachable** — `pilecap.may_be_named(actor, <row>)`, else `NotFound()` — asked before `require` (house rule 26) (`apps/core/authz.py:1695`)
- **An archived other row refuses** — `pilecap.require_live(<row>, noun="<noun>")` before every write that names it (`apps/core/verbs.py:351`)
- **Your own rows, both halves** — `for_tenant(tenant).visible_to(actor)` on every read of your org-scoped rows (house rules 8 and 24); the other app's selector scopes its own, called with the same `tenant` and `actor` (`apps/core/models.py:765`)
- **Its writes are its services'** — a change to the other app's row is a call to its service, never its model (house rule 10) (`quality/rules.yaml:1191`)

## When the other noun archives or merges

- **A live link blocks an archive** — your app drops `archive_blockers.py` with `BLOCKERS = {"<noun>": fn}`; the other app never imports yours (`apps/core/verbs.py:72`)
- **A merge carries your rows** — every foreign key into a mergeable noun is re-pointed by your `merge_repointers.py` (`REPOINTERS["<noun>"]`) or named in its `merge_keeps` with a reason — `related_name="+"` included; `djb.E074` refuses neither (`apps/core/checks.py:796`)

## Where the decision is written

- **The lead's two deliverables** — an app map row in the product's own `docs/product/architecture.md`, and an ADR file `docs/product/adrs/<app>-<n>.md` for every cross-app decision (`docs/product/architecture.md`)
- **The row's form** — `| <your app> | <Noun> (aggregate) | core, accounts, <other app> | <doors> | <workflows> | <events> |` — the arrow is the `depends_on` column (`docs/product/architecture.md`)
- **The ADR file's form** — `docs/product/adrs/<app>-<n>.md`, the id its filename, headed `# ADR <app>-<n>`, then `- **ADR <app>-<n> (<title>) · <date>** · **context:** … · **decision:** … · **rejected:** … · trigger to revisit: …` — the worked one is below (`docs/product/adrs/example_portal-1.md:3`)
- **Never a `divergence:` line** — that grammar records a product's edit to a template-owned path; `apps/` and the product's own `architecture.md` are the product's, and a link between two of your apps is a decision, not a divergence (`docs/product/build-contract.md:261`)

## What rule 7 refuses

- **An undeclared import** — an import of an app your `depends_on` does not name — read by AST off the declaration; the valve is `# rule-7: <reason>` on the flagged line or in the contiguous comment block directly above it, never further away, and a reason under 12 characters is its own finding; tests are exempt by design (`quality/rules.yaml:976`)

## What the scaffold does not write

- **No shape writes a foreign key** — `field`'s types are closed — `datetime` `date` `str` `text` `int` `bool` `decimal` `uuid` — so the field, `depends_on` and the migration are by hand, as above (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:130`)
- **`child` is one app's ledger** — `child <app> <Parent> <Child>` writes an append-only row under a noun of the SAME app, `PROTECT` to its parent; a line someone edits later is not a `child` (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/child.py:1`)

## The worked example

- **`example_portal` → `example`** — a `PortalRequest` names its `Widget` (`apps/example_portal/models.py:55`)
- **Its declaration** — `depends_on` ends `"example"` (`apps/example_portal/apps.py:36`)
- **Its service** — reach, then live, then capability (`apps/example_portal/services.py:45`)
- **Its repointer** — a widget merge carries the requests (`apps/example_portal/merge_repointers.py:26`)
- **Its record** — ADR example_portal-1 — the template's own decision log (`docs/product/adrs/example_portal-1.md:3`)
